practiceQuestions.q: What is the term used for the circular path around the stupa meant for circumambulation (Pradakshina)?
practiceQuestions.sol: The circular path enclosed by the railing for devotional circumambulation around the stupa is known as the Pradakshina Patha. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q: Which architectural feature sits at the very top of the stupa dome, symbolizing a balcony or enclosure for the sacred umbrella?
practiceQuestions.sol: Harmika is a balcony-like railing structure that is placed on top of the dome (anda) and represents a sacred enclosure. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q: In Post-Mauryan stupa architecture, what are 'Toranas'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Toranas are elaborately carved, freestanding ceremonial gateways positioned at the four cardinal points of the stupa railing. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following sites is renowned for its magnificent Post-Mauryan stone railing and gateway additions, initially built during the Maurya period?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sanchi Stupa (Stupa No. 1), originally commissioned by Ashoka, was significantly expanded in the Post-Mauryan (Sunga/Satavahana) period with stone casings, terraces (medhi), railings (vedika), and ornate gateways (toranas). [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary function of the 'Vedika' in a Buddhist stupa?
opts: To store bodily relics of the Buddha
To serve as a structural fence enclosing the sacred precinct
To act as the main entrance archway

The Vedika is a railing that encloses the stupa and the circumambulation path, physically and symbolically separating the sacred space from the secular world. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q: Amravati Stupa, famous for its white marble sculptures and narrative relief panels, is located in the valley of which river?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Amravati Stupa is located on the banks of the Krishna River in Andhra Pradesh and flourished under the Satavahana rulers. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q: What does the 'Anda' represent in the architecture of a Buddhist stupa?
opts: A hemispherical dome symbolizing the universe or cosmic mound
The meditative posture of the Buddha

practiceQuestions.sol: The Anda is the large hemispherical solid dome of the stupa, symbolizing the cosmic mountain or the dome of heaven. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q: Which dynasty is predominantly credited with the addition of rich stone carvings, vedikas, and toranas to the Sanchi Stupa during the Post-Mauryan period?

practiceQuestions.sol: While the brick core of Sanchi Stupa was built by Ashoka (Maurya), the wooden railings were replaced by stone, and magnificent toranas were added during the Sunga and subsequently Satavahana periods. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the term for the vertical pillars of the stupa railing (vedika)?

practiceQuestions.sol: In a vedika, the vertical posts are called stambhas or thambhas, through which horizontal crossbars known as 'suchi' pass. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which stylistic school of art is particularly famous for using white Palnad limestone for stupa sculptures in the Krishna-Godavari delta?

practiceQuestions.sol: The Amaravati school of art prominently used white Palnad marble/limestone to create intricate narrative panels and sculptures on stupas like Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the transition from Mauryan wooden architecture to Post-Mauryan stone architecture manifest in stupa construction?
opts: By completely abandoning hemispherical domes in favor of square towers
By replicating wooden carpentry techniques (mortise and tenon joints) in stone railings and gateways
By replacing stone cores entirely with brick and mud mortar
By eliminating the pradakshina patha and restricting access to monks only
practiceQuestions.sol: Post-Mauryan stone structures such as railings (vedikas) and gateways (toranas) consciously imitated earlier wooden prototypes, evident in joinery details like mortise and tenon joints carved directly into the stone. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art]
